concrete_capability_transition: Brownie CLI moves from a source-tree-only binary with only global help into a practical standalone CLI surface with command-specific help and a tested local install path for the existing brownie binary.

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Makes the Brownie CLI installable into a caller-owned local prefix and discoverable through command-specific help, so headless callers and humans can invoke the existing runtime-backed entrypoint without relying on VSIX or ad hoc source-tree paths.
Provides help for progress-oriented commands such as status, inspect, list, mode, run, and resume while preserving runtime ownership of progress and next-action semantics.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development by making the CLI a practical standalone entrypoint, and supports progress_visualization by making existing runtime-backed progress commands discoverable through bounded command help.
answers.new_capability: A caller can run brownie help <topic> without runtime startup and can install the existing brownie binary into a selected local prefix, then verify the installed binary with brownie --version.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before CLI-8, the binary had only top-level help and no tested local install path; operators had to rely on source-tree cargo artifacts and could not inspect command-specific syntax without external documentation.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: CLI-9 and CLI-10 would depend on ad hoc source-tree invocation rather than a supported installed binary and users would lack command-specific help required for standalone CLI product completion.
answers.non_duplicative: CLI-5.1 fixed run identity and scoped resume, CLI-6 added progress and mode UX, and CLI-7 stabilized JSON and exit codes. CLI-8 changes installability and help discoverability, not runtime execution semantics or output projections.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. Help and installation are CLI-local executable behavior and use no new runtime JSON-RPC method or passthrough.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds command behavior, installer tests, and supporting README guidance, not a readiness, report, digest, verdict, history, inspection, or summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust runtime behavior remains unchanged; user-visible CLI behavior changes by adding brownie help <topic> and a tested repository-local install path that preserves runtime authority.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can resolve an installed brownie binary, inspect bounded command syntax without launching the runtime, and then invoke brownie run <objective> with stable prior CLI contracts.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes CLI-8 Installation / Packaging / Help and leaves CLI-9 arbitrary-repository Golden Journey plus CLI-10 restart/recovery Golden Journey as the remaining required gaps.

phase makes develop the primary command
phase makes the CLI select tasks, rank continuation candidates, read ledgers directly, or own recovery/replay policy

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: CLI-8 updates the deterministic current phase manifest and package scripts. Review must confirm the PR changes executable CLI help and local install behavior without weakening the phase-value guard or adding wrapper-only surfaces.

exit_criteria: brownie help run documents brownie run <objective> as the primary execution entry and does not introduce develop.
brownie help resume, status, inspect, list, and mode provide bounded command-specific syntax and runtime-boundary notes.
brownie help <unknown> fails with invalid invocation exit code 64 and bounded human/JSON error semantics.
Help and version commands succeed without BROWNIE_RUNTIME_PATH and do not launch the runtime.
brownie run --help treats --help as objective text while brownie help run is the command-help surface.
The installer supports deterministic dry-run validation for a selected local prefix without creating prefix/bin.
The installer rejects relative, root, parent-traversal-normalizing, and common system prefixes before mutation.
A temporary-prefix install can copy the existing brownie binary and the installed binary answers --version without the VSIX.
README documents the tested install path and basic CLI usage as supporting evidence, not as documentation-only completion.
No new runtime RPC, generic passthrough, report, readiness, history, digest, verdict, summary, CLI-owned policy engine, or workspace mutation authority is introduced.
behavior_evidence: brownie-cli parser and process tests cover command-specific help topics and unknown topic failure.
brownie-cli tests prove help succeeds without runtime path configuration and does not mention develop.
brownie-cli tests prove brownie run --help remains objective payload while brownie help run renders help.
installer node tests cover dry-run output, prefix validation, temporary-prefix install, and installed --version execution.

accepted_capability: The Brownie CLI exposes command-specific help without starting the runtime.
The Brownie CLI has a tested repository-local install path into a caller-owned prefix.
behavior_evidence: Rust CLI tests cover command help, runtime-free help behavior, run objective token preservation, and bounded invalid-help failure.
Node installer tests cover dry-run, validation, local-prefix install, and installed --version.
safety_boundary: No Core Runtime terminal campaign state is reopened or mutated.
No new runtime JSON-RPC method is added.
The CLI does not read ledgers, discover Mode Packs from files, evaluate permissions, select tasks, apply patches, or own recovery policy.
Installer mutation is limited to an explicitly selected caller-owned prefix and rejects common system prefixes.
non_goals: No Homebrew formula, npm publication, signed release artifacts, notarization, or global package publication.
No arbitrary-repository Golden Journey or restart/recovery Golden Journey closure.
No Mode Pack, Product DoD, provider, permission, workspace mutation, replay, or fail-closed semantic redesign.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected repurposing brownie run --help because tokens after run must remain objective text.
Rejected documentation-only completion because installation and help must be executable and tested.
Rejected global package publication because CLI-8 only needs a practical local install path before Golden Journey validation.
Rejected a runtime help RPC because command syntax and local installer behavior are CLI concerns while runtime policy stays Rust-owned.
technical_debt: CLI-9 must validate the arbitrary-repository Golden Journey using the installed CLI path.
CLI-10 must validate restart/recovery including scoped resume and runtime-owned recovery provenance.
next_capability_rationale: After CLI-8 lands, proceed to CLI-9 General Arbitrary-Repository Golden Journey rather than adding packaging variants.
